# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 83 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 83 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_083_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8 — The Names of the Virgins

**1** "What is the name of the Son of God?" I asked. "His name is vast and without limit," he said, "and it holds up the entire world. If the whole creation is held together by the Son of God, think what that means for those who carry his name, who walk according to his instructions. **2** You see whom he upholds — those who carry his name with complete commitment. He became the very foundation beneath them, and he bears them gladly, because they are never ashamed of his name." **3** "Tell me the names of the virgins," I said, "and those women dressed in black." **4** "The four principal virgins who stand at the corners," he said, "are named: Faith, Self-Control, Strength, and Endurance. The remaining ones standing between them are named: Simplicity, Innocence, Holiness, Joy, Truth, Discernment, Harmony, and Love. **5** These qualities belong to everyone who carries the name of the Son of God and follows his ways." **6** "And the women in black — what are their names?" **7** "They are also ten: Unbelief, Excess, Disobedience, Deception, Grief, Wickedness, Lust, Bitterness, Dishonesty, and Hatred. Anyone serving God who is characterized by these things may catch a glimpse of God's kingdom, but will not enter it." **8** "And the stones that were rejected and didn't fit into the tower — who are they?" **9** "These were genuine believers who lived holy, upright lives — but they carried these destructive character traits. So they were rejected from the tower as unfit for construction. They were damaging to other believers trying to live rightly; that's why they were cast out and handed over to the women in black. They won't enter the tower until they shed those harmful patterns."

---

*PNEUMA renders virtues and vices in contemporary character language: "Self-Control" for Continence, "Strength" for Power, "Discernment" for Understanding.*
